newsitem.title: ITALY: INSTANT VIEW - Italy Oct CPI seen at 3.1 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Italy Oct CPI seen at 3.1 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on data from three sample cities indicating Italian consumer price inflation in October at an annual 3.1 percent and a month-on-month rate of 0.1 percent.
An earlier Reuter poll of analysts saw on average October CPI coming in at 3.2 percent year-on-year with a month-on-month rise of 0.3 percent.
The September annual rate was 3.4 percent.
"I think that given what we've seen for these three cities, we'll see 0.2-0.3 percent month/month and 3.1-3.2 percent year/year," said Riccardo Barbieri at Morgan Stanley in Milan.

Mario Noera, chief economist at Deutsche Bank in Milan said: "It's favourable, just for the prospects in the short term for having a lower discount rate. The Bank of Italy will probably cut (the discount rate) when inflation falls under three percent. The chances of having three percent inflation earlier than expected are incresing."
Sharda Persaud, economist at San Paolo bank in London: "We expect 75-100 basis points off the discount rate this time next month."

Noera: "A lot of exceptional factors played a role in this data -- a reduction in phone tariffs, flight tickets. In general the first three cities give a good indication because they account for 43.6 percent of the total...I think a reduction in the discount rate could be more substantial than expected -- 75 to 100 basis points."

Rodolfo Dozio, economist at Banca Commerciale Italiana: "If even six of the remaining seven sample cities were to show a monthly rate of 0.4 percent, the year-on-year rate would not go above 3.2 percent." The bank's own forecast is 3.1 percent.
